title: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB pack on vLLM (NVIDIA's recipe)
slug_note: NVIDIA's own vLLM command for the 2-bit-expert 24 GB pack, with DFlash speculative decoding.

variation.quant_detail: IQ2 experts (quantisation-aware distillation) with higher-precision other layers, 24.1 GB packed
variation.revision_note: HF snapshot downloaded and served on 2026-10-25

engine.config: NVIDIA card Quick Start: vLLM nightly, b12x kernels, FP8 KV, 256K, 1 sequence, DFlash drafter (7 tokens)

requirements.notes: Estimate: the 24.1 GB pack plus the drafter and FP8 KV cache; NVIDIA lists RTX 5090, DGX Spark and RTX Spark as supported hardware. Not measured.

drop in MemAvailable from before start (OS file cache dropped) to server ready; vLLM default --gpu-memory-utilization (0.9), so this is the reservation, not the minimum the model needs

caveats: No speed or memory numbers recorded yet.
Steps 2-6 run inside the container that step 1 opens.
spec_decode is 'other': NVIDIA's DFlash method with the LiLiCorr drafter, which this directory's enum does not name.
The experts are 2-bit; NVIDIA recovers accuracy with quantisation-aware distillation, but quality at this size has not been checked here.

Fails exactly as NVIDIA wrote it (tested 2026-10-25): the pinned vllm-openai nightly image has no wget, so the parser download step stops the container. Fix: use curl -fLO (shown above). Nothing else was changed.
Works with one fix on a DGX Spark: server ready 8 min 21 s after start.

Same box, same test script (2026-10-25): SLOWER than the Ollama nemotron-3.5-bolt tag (62.9 vs 71.2 tok/s short prompt; 66.1 vs 90.1 code), while reserving about 3x the memory. Faster only on long-prompt first token (2.6 s vs 4.2 s at 4.7K tokens). The recipe pins --max-num-seqs 1, so it is tuned for one user; this is its intended case.

The unpinned `pip install b12x` pulled b12x 1.5.1, which logs that its FP6 plugin cannot register with this vLLM build. This checkpoint has no FP6 layers (Q8_0, IQ2_XXS, unquantised), so it did not matter here.

Why slower (tested 2026-10-25, same script, one change at a time): the Ollama nemotron-3.5-bolt tag ships the same kind of setup (IQ2_XXS weights plus a 1 GB drafter, 7 draft tokens). With drafting switched off, vLLM decodes the same weights at 31.1 tok/s vs Ollama 40.2 (23% slower). Drafting helps vLLM more (2.0x, to 62.9) than Ollama (1.8x, to 71.2), so the drafter is not the problem: vLLM's base kernels for this 2-bit GGUF-packed checkpoint are slower on GB10 than llama.cpp's (which Ollama uses). Swapping FLASHINFER for FLASH_ATTN is not possible here: vLLM refuses FP8 KV cache with FlashAttention on SM121.
vLLM logged a mean draft acceptance length of about 3.4-3.7 tokens per step (7 drafted).
